messages.content: I want to see the last years data for stock prices on the top 10 stocks from the Toronto stock exchange.

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve data. This function is commonly used for API calls and web scraping. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The Date Nager API provides access holiday information for over 100 countries, including the ability to query for long weekends. It leverages ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes to tailor the search to your specific region of interest. More information can be found in https://date.nager.at/Api

headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to see the last years data for stock prices on the top 10 stocks from the Toronto Stock Exchange. We need to fetch data. Likely we need to get top 10 stocks by market cap or volume. Then get historical price data for the last year. Use an API like Alpha Vantage or Yahoo Finance. But we have no direct tool for finance. We could use requests_get to call a finance API. For example, Yahoo Finance has endpoints but might require scraping. Alternatively, use Alpha Vantage free API: https://www.alphavantage.co/query?function=TIME_SERIES_DAILY_ADJUSTED&symbol=TSX:RY&apikey=demo. But we need API key. We don't have one. Could use IEX Cloud? Might need key.

We could use a public endpoint like https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v7/finance/download/RY?period1=... etc. That requires constructing period1 and period2 timestamps. We can compute epoch times for last year. But we need to do it for each symbol. We need top 10 TSX stocks. Which ones? We can approximate: Royal Bank of Canada (RY), Toronto-Dominion Bank (TD), Enbridge Inc (ENB), Canadian National Railway (CNR), Suncor Energy (SU), Brookfield Asset Management (BAM.A), Manulife Financial (MFC), Bank of Nova Scotia (BNS), Canadian Natural Resources (CNQ), and perhaps BCE Inc (BCE). These are typical top TSX by market cap. So we can fetch data for each symbol.

We need to call requests_get for each symbol. We'll need to compute period1 and period2. Let's compute period1 as timestamp for one year ago from today. Today is 2026-10-18. One year ago is 2025-10-18. Convert to epoch. 2025-10-18 00:00:00 UTC. That's about 173... Let's compute approximate epoch: 2025-10-18 is around 173... Actually let's compute precisely: 2025-10-18 is after 2025-01-01. 2025-01-01 epoch is 1735689600. Add days: Oct 18 is day 291 of 2025 (since 2025 is not leap year). So add 290 days *86400 = 25056000. Sum = 1761744000. So period1 ~ 1761744000. Period2 is now: 2026-10-18 epoch: 2026-01-01 epoch is 1767225600. Add 290 days: 25056000. Sum = 1792281600. So period2 ~ 1792281600.

We can use Yahoo Finance download endpoint: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v7/finance/download/{symbol}?period1={period1}&period2={period2}&interval=1d&events=history&includeAdjustedClose=true

We need to pass symbol like RY. For TSX, sometimes need suffix .NS? Actually Yahoo uses RY.TO for TSX. So we should use RY.TO, TD.TO, ENB.TO, CNR.TO, SU.TO, BAM.A.TO? Actually BAM.A is on TSX but maybe use BAM.A.TO. MFC.TO, BNS.TO, CNQ.TO, BCE.TO.

So we can call requests_get for each symbol. We'll parse CSV. But we only need to show data. We can just return the raw CSV or parse into JSON. Let's parse into JSON array of objects with date, open, high, low, close, adj close, volume.

We'll need to handle errors. We'll loop through symbols. Use requests_get with url and params. We'll set headers Content-Type application/json. We'll set timeout 10. We'll parse response text. We'll split lines, skip header, parse each line. Build array. Then combine all into a dict mapping symbol to array.

Return JSON.
